key_insight: TrialDesignBench reveals a gap between frontier LLMs and expert-validated, contemporary standards for selecting early-phase oncology trial designs.
clinical_relevance: Better evaluation of AI-assisted design selection could support how oncology trials test doses, but this study does not establish readiness for clinical use.
method: Paired trials with expert-validated reference designs aligned with current FDA initiatives, including Project Optimus.
Evaluated five frontier LLMs and used ablations to investigate performance gaps.
evidence_signal: No evaluated LLM matched the reference standard; supplying latent design determinants increased class-wise balanced accuracy by 0.22, while structured decision-tree reasoning increased it by 0.24.
watch_item: Key design determinants may be absent from trial records, limiting reliable design selection from source documents alone.
paper_title: TrialDesignBench: Benchmarking Language Models for Phase-I Trial Design Against Clinical Knowledge
